subject: Re: Legends for width and height in geom_rect

messages.author: 40b63348dbcb447d
messages.subject: Re: Legends for width and height in geom_rect
parts:
This command will produce what I was describing, except for the legend I need.

scale <- 0.02

iris.vis <- ggplot()+geom_rect(data=iris,mapping=aes(xmin=Sepal.Length-scale*Petal.Length/2,ymin=Sepal.Width-scale*Petal.Width/2,xmax=Sepal.Length+scale*Petal.Length/2,ymax=Sepal.Width+scale*Petal.Width/2,fill=Species,color=Species),alpha=0.1)+xlab("Sepal.Length")+ylab("Sepal.Width")+theme_bw()

print(iris.vis)

On Wednesday, February 6, 2013 6:46:06 PM UTC+2, Ziyuan Lin wrote:
Hi,

I am visualizing a 4 dimensional data set. My point is to relate x and y coordinates in a scatter plot to the first 2 dimension, and draw a rectangle in each x-y position, with width and height proportional to the 3rd and the 4th dimension. It is easy to do this task with geom_rect() by specifying xmin/xmax/ymin/ymax, but I also need a legend for the width and height of the rectangles. How to do it in ggplot? Thank you.

Ziyuan
